_: THE NAMED-INDICATOR LIBRARY. One entry per named indicator: the ONE checked formula the assistant builds when a member names it (api/services/named_indicators.py says how). A person writes `formula` (with {param} where a parameter's number goes), `params`, `aliases` and `evidence`; tools/named_indicators_build.py writes `tree`, `sites` and each newest version's `maths`. THE RULE: an entry's maths never changes under the same version; a change is a new entry in its `versions` with the reason (every shipped version's fingerprint is also recorded in named_indicators_shipped.json, and a recorded one never changes). `evidence.published` is what was READ, on the date in `read`, at the pages listed; `says` is the definition in those pages' terms. Aliases are never a bare two- or three-letter acronym (an entry's `acronyms`, where it has any, are read inside the Create Indicator door only and are the initials of that entry alone). `held` lists names UCT knows and has NO checked formula for: each is refused by name with the way forward (`describe` is the rule in plain words, an example of what the member can ask for instead).

outputs.label: Laguerre Filter
outputs.says: four smoothing stages of the bar's midpoint, averaged with weights 1, 2, 2 and 1

published.says: MotiveWave's page, crediting Ehlers ('Time Warp - Without Space Travel'): l0 = alpha x price + (1 - alpha) x the previous l0; l1 = -(1 - alpha) x l0 + the previous l0 + (1 - alpha) x the previous l1, and l2 and l3 the same one stage on; the filter is (l0 + 2 x l1 + 2 x l2 + l3) / 6. Price is the midpoint and alpha is 0.2 by default; a missing previous value is read as the price.
published.note: Written with Ehlers' own gamma, the share each stage KEEPS: gamma is 1 - the page's alpha, so the default 0.8 is the page's 0.2. It is the function laguerre(source, gamma), four linked running values. Every one of them is a plain-number mix of the four, so where they started provably stops mattering; they are restarted a number of bars back that is sized from gamma (192 at 0.8), and a chart's first bars up to that number have no value. A gamma above 0.95 is not offered: the filter then remembers further back than a chart formula may reach. TradingView has no Laguerre Filter of its own; this engine's restart was checked against TradingView running these same equations carried from the first bar (equal on every bar to 1 part in a quadrillion), which is evidence about the restart, not a second opinion on the equations.

outputs.label: Laguerre RSI
outputs.says: of the gaps between four smoothing stages of the close, the share where an earlier stage is on top

published.says: MotiveWave's page, crediting Ehlers ('Time Warp - Without Space Travel'): l0 = (1 - gamma) x price + gamma x the previous l0; l1 = -gamma x l0 + the previous l0 + gamma x the previous l1, and l2 and l3 the same one stage on. For each neighbouring pair of stages the gap between them goes to cu when the earlier stage is at or above the later one and to cd otherwise; rsi = cu / (cu + cd) when that sum is not 0. Price is the close and gamma is 0.5 by default.
published.note: The page does not say that cu and cd start from 0 on each bar; this entry takes them so (carried instead, they would be running totals and the result would not be an oscillator). It runs 0 to 1, as published, not 0 to 100. It is the function laguerreRsi(source, gamma), written as 0.5 + 0.5 x (l0 - l3) / (the sum of the three gaps' sizes): the gaps telescope, so that is cu / (cu + cd), the same number. The four linked running values are a plain-number mix of each other, so where they started provably stops mattering; they are restarted a number of bars back that is sized from gamma (64 at 0.5). A gamma above 0.95 is not offered. TradingView has no Laguerre RSI of its own; this engine's restart was checked against TradingView running these same equations carried from the first bar (equal on every bar to 2 parts in 100 billion), which is evidence about the restart, not a second opinion on the equations.

outputs.label: Fisher

outputs.label: Trigger

published.by: John Ehlers (as published by Tulip Indicators)
published.says: Tulip Indicators' page, citing Ehlers (Stocks & Commodities V.20:11, 'Using the Fisher Transform'): hl = (high + low) / 2; val = 0.33 x 2 x ((hl - min) / (max - min) - 0.5) + 0.67 x the previous val, min and max over n bars of hl; fisher = 0.5 x log((1 + val) / (1 - val)) + 0.5 x the previous fisher; the signal is the previous bar's fisher. Its source code adds what the page leaves out: val above 0.99 becomes 0.999 and below -0.99 becomes -0.999. TradingView's help page gives only the transform, half the log of (1 + X) / (1 - X).
published.note: Vendors differ under this name (another publishes 0.5 and 0.5 smoothing with a quarter of the log and a 0.9999 cap). This entry is the form TradingView's built-in computes, which the capture settles bar for bar. It is written as the function fisher(length), which stands for the whole recurrence. The value it feeds back is SNAPPED, a choice on its own value, so by its shape nothing proves that where it started stops mattering, and Create Indicator refuses that shape written out by hand; the function is offered on the capture. It is recomputed from 300 bars back on every bar: the first 300 bars of a chart's history have no value, where TradingView's has one. With 300 bars of restart, a length past 659 reaches further back than any formula may, and is refused for that as any formula is.

This entry has no value on the first 300 bars of the chart's history, where TradingView's has one from the first full range: it is recomputed from 300 bars back on every bar. The trigger is the Fisher line one bar earlier.

outputs.says: the depth of pullbacks from the period's highest close, as a root-mean-square percent

published.says: Percent drawdown = (close - 14-period highest close) / that highest close x 100; squared average = 14-period sum of the squared drawdowns / 14; Ulcer Index = its square root.
published.note: The highest close includes this bar's own.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for.

outputs.label: TRIX
outputs.says: the one-bar change of a triple-smoothed EMA of the log of price, times 10,000

published.says: An EMA of the close, an EMA of that, an EMA of that; TRIX is the 1-period percent change of the triple EMA. No page read states a multiplier.
published.note: THIS ENTRY FOLLOWS TRADINGVIEW'S BUILT-IN, not the pages' wording: 10,000 x the one-bar change of a triple EMA of the LOG of price, which the capture shows is what TradingView plots (equal on every bar). The percent change of price the pages describe is about a hundredth of this size. The length default, 18, is TradingView's; the capture was taken at 15.

outputs.label: DPO
outputs.says: the close minus where its simple average stood half the length plus one bars ago

published.by: StockCharts ChartSchool (the page credits no author)
published.says: The price less an X-period simple moving average that is displaced X/2 + 1 periods (11 for 20), so that the average sits in the middle of its look-back period; the page says the oscillator is itself displaced to the left, so its last values do not line up with the latest prices. 20 periods by default.
published.note: THIS ENTRY FOLLOWS TRADINGVIEW'S BUILT-IN in its default (not centred) form, not the page's: the close minus its simple average AS IT STOOD floor(length / 2) + 1 bars ago, drawn on the bar it is computed on. The captures show that is what TradingView plots, equal on every bar, at an odd length (21, 11 bars back) and an even one (20, also 11). The textbook form the page describes reads the PRICE that many bars back against today's average and is drawn shifted into the past (TradingView's Centered option): a different number on every bar. The bars-back count is derived from the length, which is why the formula is the function dpo(source, length). The default length, 21, is TradingView's.

capture.detail: Equal on every bar both charts have a value for. Graded at length 21 (run builtin2-2026-11-18, the same two charts) and at length 20 (this run), Centered off at both. One bar more or less of displacement disagrees on nearly every bar, and so does the Centered capture.

follows.what: the close minus its simple average from half the length plus one bars ago
follows.others: The textbook form is drawn shifted into the past and differs.

outputs.label: Pocket Pivot
outputs.formula: close > close[1] && (close - low) / (high - low) >= 0.5 && highest(close < close[1] ? 1 : 0, 10)[1] > 0 && volume > highest(close < close[1] ? volume : 0, 10)[1] && close >= sma(close, 50) && close >= sma(close, 200) && low <= sma(close, 10) && close > close[105]
outputs.says: true on an up day closing in its top half on more volume than any down day of the prior 10, in an uptrend, not stretched

house.whose: UCT's own Pocket Pivot, the one the Screener's base structures use
house.what: Morales and Kacher's volume rule with their stated conditions
house.note: Six tests, every one a fact of the bar: an up day; the close in the top half of the bar's range; at least one down day in the 10 sessions before, and volume above the largest volume of those down days; the close at or above its 50- and 200-day simple averages; the low not above the 10-day average; the close above where it was 105 bars ago. The numbers are the detector's own and are not settings. What the authors leave to judgement (the fundamentals, a constructive base) is not in the detector and is not in this formula.
